subject: Decision tradeoffs & sandbox test plan (post-discovery)
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Leah Park <leah.park@nimbulahealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Decision tradeoffs & sandbox test plan (post-discovery)

Leah / Jeff — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick post-call recap so we’re aligned and we can get the sandbox rolling next week.

TL;DR
- Primary pains you called out: latency spikes during batch ingest, unpredictable per-token cost at scale, and audit/logging gaps for regulated workflows.
- Primary goals: predictable sub-150ms median latency for short instructions, predictable monthly cost within 20% variance, and full audit logs retained 90+ days.

What we discussed (short):
- Current setup: hybrid with sensitive data on-prem, burst workloads to cloud; you need an inference layer that can failover gracefully and give provable isolation.
- Decision tradeoffs: latency vs cost (larger batch sizes reduce cost but increase tail latency); quantization/FP16 options we can recommend after early runs.

Proposed sandbox / smoke-tests (attached as sandbox-test-cases.xlsx):
1) Throughput baseline: 50 RPS sustained for 30 minutes, measure P50/P95/P99 latency and GPU utilization.
2) Burst resilience: sudden +3x traffic for 5 minutes with autoscale policy to simulate morning batch windows.
3) On-prem sync: validate VPC peering and local model hosting with a 2-node setup (data residency test).
4) Audit/logging: generate 1M events, verify retention + retrieval speed for last-90-day range.

Asks / next steps:
- Leah: confirm priority ranking for the four tests above (we heard throughput and on-prem first, but want written confirmation).
- Jeff: can you share a sandbox account that allows a small S3 bucket and one EC2/GPU instance? If you prefer, we can run a Redwood-managed sandbox in your VPC (we’ll send a template and architecture doc).
- Camila / Marissa (cc): once we have the environment, can you lead the setup and own the test run? I’ll coordinate with Nimbula’s engineering calendar.

Attachments: sandbox-test-cases.xlsx (test matrix), redwood-sandbox-setup-guide.pdf (architecture + IAM checklist).

Thanks — aiming to get the first run scheduled by next Tuesday.

— Avery
Avery Johnson

Thanks Avery — great recap and clear next steps. Confirming a few priorities from our side so we don’t diverge:

Priority order (from our execs/infra):
1) Data residency / on‑prem option (must be demonstrable during POC)
2) Auditability & long retention for logs (HIPAA + internal compliance)
3) Burst handling / graceful failover (we have predictable batch windows)
4) Unit cost predictability (we want to avoid large per-token swings during bursts)

Two requests you flagged that we need explicit comparisons on before we proceed:
- Can you provide a short competitor snapshot on on‑prem readiness and licensing (we’re evaluating NimbusAI and CloudPrompt in parallel)?
- Also we require clarity on billing model: true committed throughput pricing vs pure per-token usage. Our procurement will push for a committed option if feasible.

We can provision a test S3 + one p3.2xlarge for the first pass — Jeff will confirm the exact IAM roles. In the meantime, please send the competitor snapshot and proposed timeline for the three test cycles (smoke, full run, regression).

Leah — thanks for the clear priorities. I put together a short competitor snapshot and a proposed 10‑day sandbox cadence (attached: competitive-matrix.csv + quick test schedule in this message).

Quick competitor snapshot (high level):
- NimbusAI: strong on latency for cloud-first workloads, limited off‑the‑shelf on‑prem packaging — mostly professional services. Licensing tends to be per‑node with upfront minimums.
- CloudPrompt: offers on‑prem via an appliance partner, but their audit/log pipeline is slower (log ingestion lag ~30–60min) and retention tiers cost extra. Billing is flexible per-token but less attractive for committed throughput.
- Redwood (summary): engineered for both hosted and private runtimes; we can run a customer‑owned on‑prem instance with a private control plane and provide both per‑token and committed throughput options in the Dedicated SKU (we’ll surface a committed throughput term sheet if you want it).

Proposed 10‑day sandbox cadence: (we can compress or expand as needed)
Day 0: Environment handoff — S3 bucket, one GPU instance (or VPC peering for on‑prem), IAM roles exchanged.
Day 1–2: Quick smoke (sanity checks, baseline P50/P95).
Day 3–4: Throughput baseline run (50 RPS sustained), collect GPU telemetry.
Day 5: Midweek regression run + burst test (+3x traffic for 5 minutes).
Day 6–7: On‑prem sync validation and audit log ingestion at scale.
Day 8–9: Tuning (batching, quantization config) and final pass.
Day 10: Readout + short decision memo for your stakeholders.

Owners (proposed):
- Redwood setup & run: Camila (setup) + Avery (test runs)
- Nimbula sandbox & IAM: Jeff (provide creds)
- Compliance readout & retention verification: Leah + Nimbula infra

Attachments: competitive-matrix.csv (short comparison), sandbox-test-cases.xlsx (already sent) — I also attached a short PDF on Redwood Private/SLA options in case your procurement team wants it.
